title: Campaign: non-invasive brain measurement, probing with diffuse light
abstract: Subcampaign of 'how can human brain activity be measured without surgery, better than today?'. Scope: Near-infrared light sent into the head and detected after scattering: continuous, frequency- and time-domain diffuse optics, diffuse correlation and speckle methods. 51 papers. Status: mostly bounds. Published fast optical signals need 0.3-19% cortical scattering changes, far above 0.02-0.1% from animal data, and physiological (not photon) noise limits detection. Time gating keeps most depth information with few gates (six gates within 8% of the full record in one model). Corrections for CSF layers reduce errors in brain-flow estimates (maximum error from 2.91 to 0.91 points) but leave absolute flow biased. Many results hold only in flat or spherical layered models.
